description: Strategies for detecting and handling outliers in datasets

detection_methods.name: IQR Method (Tukey Fences)
detection_methods.best_for: Skewed distributions, robust to extreme values
detection_methods.explanation: Uses the interquartile range to define boundaries. Values outside 1.5×IQR from Q1/Q3 are flagged. Robust because it's based on quartiles, not mean/std.

detection_methods.name: Z-Score Method
detection_methods.explanation: Assumes normal distribution. Values beyond 3 standard deviations from the mean are flagged. Not suitable for skewed data.

detection_methods.name: Modified Z-Score (MAD)
detection_methods.best_for: Robust alternative to Z-score, works with skewed data
detection_methods.explanation: Uses Median Absolute Deviation instead of standard deviation. More robust to the presence of outliers themselves.

treatment_patterns.name: Extreme Outliers in Revenue/Financial Data
treatment_patterns.explanation: Winsorizing caps extreme values at a percentile (e.g., 1st and 99th). This preserves the record while reducing the outlier's influence on aggregates.
treatment_patterns.business_impact: Uncapped revenue outliers can inflate average order value by 30-50%, misleading pricing and inventory decisions.
treatment_patterns.example: Winsorized 23 revenue values exceeding $50,000 (99th percentile cap) — these outlier transactions inflated average order value from $245 to $890.

treatment_patterns.name: Outliers in Age/Demographic Data
treatment_patterns.explanation: Physically impossible values (negative age, age > 120) are data entry errors, not natural outliers. These must be reviewed, not statistically treated.
treatment_patterns.business_impact: Invalid ages corrupt customer segmentation, age-based pricing models, and compliance with age-restricted product regulations.
treatment_patterns.example: ⚠️ Found 8 records with age > 150 and 3 with age < 0 — these are data entry errors, not outliers. Flagged for manual correction.

treatment_patterns.name: Natural Outliers in Salary Data
treatment_patterns.condition: Salary/income column with legitimate high values (executives, senior roles)
treatment_patterns.explanation: Executive salaries are real outliers driven by business hierarchy. Removing them would lose legitimate data. Use RobustScaler (based on median/IQR) instead of StandardScaler.
treatment_patterns.business_impact: Removing executive salaries biases compensation analysis downward and makes benchmarking inaccurate for leadership hiring.
treatment_patterns.example: Kept 15 executive salary outliers (>$200K) — these are legitimate. Applied RobustScaler to normalize without distortion.

treatment_patterns.name: Outliers in Sensor/IoT Data
treatment_patterns.condition: Sensor readings with sudden spikes or impossible values
treatment_patterns.explanation: Sensor spikes are often electrical noise or measurement errors. A rolling median filter smooths these while preserving genuine trends.
treatment_patterns.business_impact: Unfiltered sensor outliers trigger false alarms in manufacturing, causing unnecessary production line shutdowns costing $10K-50K per incident.
treatment_patterns.example: Applied 5-point rolling median filter to 'temperature_sensor' — removed 67 noise spikes while preserving the genuine temperature upward trend.

treatment_patterns.name: Outliers for ML Model Preparation
treatment_patterns.condition: Preparing features for linear models (Linear Regression, SVM, KNN)
treatment_patterns.explanation: Linear models and distance-based algorithms are sensitive to outliers. RobustScaler uses median and IQR, making it resistant to outlier influence.
treatment_patterns.business_impact: Using StandardScaler with outliers present degrades linear model accuracy by 10-25%. RobustScaler preserves model performance.
treatment_patterns.example: Applied RobustScaler because extreme outliers detected in 3 features — this preserves model accuracy for the downstream linear regression pipeline.

treatment_patterns.name: Outliers for Tree-Based Models
treatment_patterns.condition: Preparing features for Decision Trees, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM
treatment_patterns.explanation: Tree-based models split data at thresholds and are inherently robust to outliers. Removing outliers is unnecessary and may lose valuable information.
treatment_patterns.business_impact: No treatment needed — tree-based models handle outliers natively, preserving prediction accuracy.
treatment_patterns.example: No outlier treatment applied — dataset will be used with XGBoost which handles outliers natively through threshold-based splits.

decision_tree: 1. Are values physically impossible (negative age, 0 weight)? → Flag as invalid, manual review
2. Are outliers in financial/revenue data? → Winsorize at 1st/99th percentile
3. Are outliers legitimate (executive salaries, enterprise deals)? → Keep + use RobustScaler
4. Is this sensor/IoT data? → Apply rolling median filter
5. Is the downstream model tree-based? → No treatment needed
6. Is the downstream model linear/distance-based? → Apply RobustScaler
7. Are outliers rare and extreme? → Consider removal only if <1% of data
